name: Universidad Pontificia Comillas (ICADE)
summary: Private pontifical university in Madrid; four bachelor's taught entirely in English, in business (ICADE) and international relations.

ib.text: If your last two years are abroad: apply with your school record plus an SAT or PAA score. No minimum grade; once admitted you must meet Spain's legal university-access requirements.

programmes.name: Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration and Management [ADE] (E-2 English)
programmes.about: A flexible business degree in English at Comillas ICADE: marketing, accounting and finance, management, economics and quantitative methods, with internships and optional double degrees abroad.
programmes.overview: The first year covers management, accounting, business and financial mathematics, data analysis and microeconomics, and later years add statistics, marketing, macroeconomics, operations, organisational behaviour, corporate finance, strategy, market research and human resources. In the final year you choose electives in marketing, management, finance and accounting, or economics, complete a compulsory company placement and write a final project. Exchanges at partner universities are common, and double degrees with universities in the United States and Europe are offered. Graduates work in management, strategy consulting, corporate finance, marketing, international trade or their own ventures.
programmes.selectionNote: International applicants are judged on their school record and SAT or PAA score (College Board code 12802). 60 seats.

programmes.name: Bachelor's Degree in Business Analytics (E-8)
programmes.about: New at ICADE and taught entirely in English: finance, marketing, economics and operations combined with statistics, programming, machine learning and big data.
programmes.overview: Algebra, calculus, programming, economics and business fundamentals come first, followed by statistics, databases, financial accounting and introductory machine learning, then big data, cybersecurity, marketing analytics and quantitative finance. The last year adds deep learning and artificial intelligence, electives such as fintech, customer intelligence, sustainability measurement and supply chain analytics, a compulsory work placement and a final project. Case studies drawn from real business settings run through the course, and a double degree with international relations is available. Graduates become data analysts, machine learning specialists, strategy consultants or investment advisers.
programmes.selectionNote: International applicants are judged on their school record and SAT or PAA score (College Board code 12802). 45 seats.

programmes.name: Bachelor's Degree in International Relations
programmes.about: Geopolitics, the international economy, diplomacy and global governance, taught entirely in English, with optional double degrees through American and Asia-Pacific programmes.
programmes.overview: The course starts with law, political theory and the history of international relations, then adds comparative political systems, public international law, geopolitics, international political economy and climate governance. Later years cover international organisations, security, European Union institutions, regional studies of Africa and Latin America, trade and investment, and end with a final project. Language training runs for up to four years, work placements are available, and you can spend a semester at a partner university. Double degrees run through programmes in the Americas and Asia-Pacific. Graduates work in diplomacy, international organisations, think tanks and consultancies.
programmes.selectionNote: International applicants are judged on their school record and SAT or PAA score (College Board code 12802). 40 seats.

programmes.name: Dual Degree in Global Communication and International Relations
programmes.about: Two degrees in five years in English: international relations with global communication, two further languages, a third year abroad and a month in Brussels.
programmes.overview: Two degrees share one curriculum, with early years in political theory, international relations, communication theory, law and economics, plus two further languages. The entire third year is spent at a university abroad, with a three-week immersion in Brussels on the EU institutions. Years four and five let you specialise in economics and business, law and diplomacy, or security and human rights, with external internships and a thesis for each degree. A second exchange in the final year is optional. Graduates work as diplomats, international civil servants, policy analysts, communications directors and consultants.
programmes.selectionNote: International applicants are judged on their school record and SAT or PAA score (College Board code 12802). 40 seats.

separateFrom.name: Bachelor's Degree in International Relations
separateFrom.reason: A five-year double degree with Global Communication: a second degree, two extra languages, a year abroad and a higher fee.

notes: Comillas sets no minimum grade: it weighs your last three years' record and the admission test, and some programmes add an interview.
Programmes listed as 'English, Spanish' (ADE international, the E-3, E-5 and E-6 dual degrees) mix both languages and are not listed here.
